I am 73 years old and have farmed this land in Quzhou for 55 years. I only finished primary school, but I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. My household has seven people, but my sons and their wives work in the city most of the year, so it is mainly my wife and me in the fields, with help only during busy times when they come back. Money is tight, so I do not waste inputs, but I also will not cut so much that I risk a bad year.

This year I will keep the same layout as last year: 7 mu for wheat-maize double cropping, and 3.1 mu for cotton. I thought about planting less cotton because my back is not what it used to be and cotton needs a lot of spraying and hand-picking, but my neighbor Lao Zhang did well with cotton last year and the price was acceptable, so I will keep the 3.1 mu. The wheat-maize system is my staple — it feeds the family and gives steady income.

For winter wheat, I will rotary till the 7 mu in early October and sow improved seed, maybe Jimai 22 or something similar from the town seed shop. I will put down about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 3.5 kg of potassium. My neighbor tried less fertilizer last year and his wheat looked yellow and yielded poorly, so I will not cut back. I will irrigate three times — wintering water, jointing, and grain filling — because the well water costs me electricity money but three times is the minimum for safe yield. I will spray pesticide three times: herbicide at planting, and one or two more if I see aphids in spring. I expect about 480 kg per mu. I am old now; I do not chase record yields, I want stability.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is only a few days, so there is no time for tillage — I plant no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble, like everyone else in the village now. I buy hybrid seed, usually Denghai 605, because hybrid maize gives much better yield even if the seed is expensive. I will apply about 10 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice, at the big trumpet stage and at silking. If I see armyworm I will spray once or twice. I expect about 520 kg per mu.

For cotton, planted in late April on the 3.1 mu after rotary tillage. I use improved cotton seed. Cotton is hard work — I will need to spray about 10 times through the season for bollworm, aphids, and weeds. I will irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. For fertilizer I will use about 8 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. It is a lot of labor for an old man, but my wife and I can manage 3.1 mu, and the cotton cash helps when my sons send less money home. I expect about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I do not change much from year to year. What has worked for decades is good enough. I just want to get through the season without trouble, have enough grain for the family, and sell the rest for cash.
